title: docs(releases): v17.mdx has no 17.3.0 section and no Upgrade checklist for 17.2.0 either — two releases shipped without upgrade guidance
body:
17.3.0 published today. `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` does not mention it.

## The measured gap

| version | Highlights | detail section | **Upgrade checklist** |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 17.0.0 | ✅ `:36` | ✅ `:209` | ✅ (inside 17.1.0's, `:3952`) |
| 17.1.0 | ✅ `:113` | ✅ `:3387` | ✅ `:3952` |
| 17.2.0 | ✅ `:155` | ❌ **none** | ❌ **none** |
| 17.3.0 | ❌ **none** | ❌ **none** | ❌ **none** |

So it is not only the new release. **17.2.0 shipped with Highlights and nothing else**, and the omission has now compounded: an app on 17.1.0 upgrading today crosses two releases and the docs offer an upgrade checklist for neither.

That is not hypothetical — `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` is pinned at exactly 17.1.0 and is being upgraded right now (hotcrm#1576).

## This is the sanctioned moment and the sanctioned vehicle

`CLAUDE.md` / AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails: release notes are written **centrally, at release time** — never accreted one PR at a time, because `releases/v<major>.mdx` is the repo's hottest merge-conflict magnet. What is forbidden is a **rider on a code PR**. The guardrail's own escape hatch is the one this card takes:

> If a releases page has a factual error, file an issue or make it a **dedicated docs-only PR** — never a rider on code changes.

⛔ So: **this PR touches `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` and nothing else.** No code, no changeset (`skip-changeset`), no drive-by fixes elsewhere in `content/docs/`.

## Where the content comes from — measurement, not a reading of 862 changesets

Two inputs, in this order of authority:

1. **hotcrm#1576's breakage log.** That card upgrades a real app 17.1.0 → 17.3.0 and is required to record every breakage — symptom, verbatim error, upstream cause, fix — *including the ones that turned out to be non-issues*. That log is the Upgrade checklist's spine, because every line in it is something that actually happened to an app rather than something a changeset warned might.
2. **The changesets themselves**, for the entries hotcrm's shape never touches (it is one app; it does not exercise MongoDB, Turso, clustering, SCIM/SSO, or the cloud control plane). `spec` alone carries 57 BREAKING entries across the two releases; `client`, `cli`, `runtime`, `rest`, the drivers and `plugin-*` carry more.

⚠️ **Do not invent migration steps.** A checklist line must trace to either (1) something measured, or (2) a changeset's own Migration section. A step nobody has run is worse than a missing step: it sends upgraders to do work whose effect nobody has verified.

## Entries whose blast radius is known to reach an app

Starting set, not a scope limit:

- **`client.projects.*` → `client.environments.*`** (`87042b5`, ADR-0006 D2) — **no aliases, by decision**; response keys move; `os environments --format json` breaks. The changeset carries a full method/key migration table already written — reuse it, do not paraphrase it.
- **`plugin-auth` audience posture** collapses to `invite_only | email_domain | open`, **default `invite_only`** (`4f24e9d`) — changes behaviour for a deployment that relied on open registration.
- **Permission-store read failure now fails LOUD** (`6a180e4`) — a deployment quietly running degraded starts erroring.
- **`sys_record_share` is tenant-scoped**; pre-existing grant rows need attention (`3f64fe6`).
- **`automation/:name/toggle` now requires `manage_metadata`** (`266436a`).
- **Drivers now enforce declared `unique` / `indexes[]`** (`56c093c`, `b7f645a`) — writes that used to land silently are refused. Most likely to present as "our seed data stopped loading".

## Acceptance

- A **17.2.0** detail section and a **17.3.0** detail section, following the shape 17.0.0/17.1.0 already establish (Breaking changes & migration → New capabilities → Upgrade checklist).
- An **Upgrade checklist covering 17.1.0 → 17.3.0 as one path**, since that is the jump real deployments are making. Where a step only applies to one of the two hops, say which.
- Every checklist line traceable to a measurement or a changeset Migration section — cite the changeset hash or the hotcrm finding.
- ⛔ `content/docs/releases/` only; ⛔ nothing else in the diff; ⛔ no code.
- ⛔ Do not rewrite or "tidy" the existing 17.0.0 / 17.1.0 sections. They are the published record.

**Blocked-by: hotcrm#1576** — file this now so the gap is recorded, but write it against that card's measured log rather than ahead of it.
